target.name: Lumina Vehicles
target.founder: Ahmed Shubber (CEO; Fairfield U double-major mech + biomedical eng), Federico Di Palma (Co-founder)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $8M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Lumina Vehicles is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $8M+ to date, founded by Ahmed Shubber (CEO with dual degrees in mechanical and biomedical engineering) and Federico Di Palma. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including stage-adjacent companies like Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $8M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A progression, implying a valuation of $16M. The peer-median method examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B and a range of $1.1B to $1.8B, implying $1.6B for Lumina.

The triangulated analysis produces a wide range from $14M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $833M. This wide dispersion reflects the material tension between stage-appropriate capital-based valuation ($16M) and peer comparable valuations that span from seed to Series B, introducing significant stage and growth-rate uncertainty. Key unknowns include Lumina's specific growth trajectory, capital efficiency relative to peers, and time to next financing event. The range supports valuations between $14M–$1.9B, with material downside risk if stage-progression dynamics dominate and material upside contingent on peer-level growth execution.
